title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs
seoTitle: Paris cost of living and school protests

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating over soaring living costs and inadequate school funding.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better schools, higher wages, and pensions.
tea.changed: Oct 28: The Chamber of Commerce reported widespread business revenue drops and thousands of damaged storefronts across multiple cities.

summary: Mass demonstrations and marches erupted across Paris and other French cities, drawing hundreds of thousands of participants over rising living costs and school funding. The movement, which originated from high school staff shortages, grew to include students and workers seeking higher wages and pensions. While many demonstrations began peacefully, clashes developed near endpoints in cities including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, and Bordeaux, with some protesters throwing projectiles and police deploying tear gas, water cannons, and stun grenades. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported thousands of arrests and numerous injured officers nationwide, while retail associations highlighted severe economic losses and extensive property damage. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, blaming criminal elements and extremist groups for orchestrating the destruction, whereas opposition figures criticized the government's response.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez deployed up to 70,000 officers backed by armored vehicles, helicopters, and water cannons. Police used tear gas, sound grenades, and water cannons to disperse crowds, resulting in over 1,000 nationwide arrests according to authorities.

crowd.text: The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000.

arrests.text: Nationally, according to authorities, arrests have exceeded 1,200

injuries.text: the Interior Minister, Laurent Nuñez, denounced “very serious disturbances” during which 60 policemen were injured.

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Clashes broke out in Paris and other French cities as hundreds of thousands marched over school funding and living costs.
The French retail chamber reported massive revenue drops and over 2,500 damaged shops across the country due to ongoing unrest.
Reports confirmed one protester fatality from cardiac arrest in Paris and a severe hand injury caused by a police grenade in Saint-Étienne.
